evidence: "In the canonical operating point — low batch — decode sits in the bandwidth-bound regime. It is like pushing the water of that same 140 GB reservoir through a standard garden hose. On a single device, the full 140 GB must stream within each 25 ms step to produce one token" (printed p. 22); then on printed p. 16: "the canonical 8×H100 host each GPU streams only its 17.5 GB shard — 17.5×10^9 B read against 3.35×10^12 B/s over the 0.025 s step, or ~21% of peak bandwidth".
issue: The §2.2 Mental Model still anchors its decode metaphor on the single-device 140 GB / 25 ms framing, while the chapter's own opening (printed p. 16) insists the 8×H100 host's binding terms are TP collectives, kernel efficiency, sampling, scheduling and the ~9.2K KV read — not the weight read (~21% of peak). The chapter explicitly states the 'bandwidth-bound' verdict from 5.6 TB/s vs 3.35 TB/s is 'the hypothetical whole-model-on-one-GPU case', yet §2.2 re-narrates it as the canonical mental model, and the sentence 'the diameter of the hose (HBM bandwidth) physically cannot move that volume of water in that time frame' reasserts the saturation verdict the opening section disclaims.
fix_instruction: In §2.2's decode paragraph, replace the 140 GB / 25 ms garden-hose sentence with the sharded per-GPU statement (~17.5 GB shard, ~5.2 ms at peak, ~21% of the 25 ms step) and add a one-line pointer that the whole-model-on-one-device 140 GB/5.6 TB/s case is the hypothetical single-device roofline illustration, not the canonical host verdict. Keep the operating-point caveat, but do not let the metaphor contradict the chapter's stated binding terms.

evidence: Printed p. 87: "one H100 sustains ~2,472 tok/s at 35% MFU". Printed p. 88: "the 8-GPU host needs ~0.47 s (9,200 ÷ 19,780 = 0.465 s; 19,780 = 8 × 2,472.5 tok/s)". Printed p. 88 again: "the host's capacity screen is the ~19,800 tok/s sustained-planning rate at 35% MFU".
issue: The per-GPU sustained-planning prefill rate is quoted as ~2,472 tok/s on one page and 2,472.5 tok/s on the next; the corresponding host figure is ~19,800 tok/s in two places and 19,780 tok/s in the explicit 8 × 2,472.5 derivation. The exact value is 8 × 0.989e15 × 0.35 ÷ 140e9 = 19,780 tok/s; ~19,800 is the rounded form and 19,780 the exact form, but the text never says the 19,800 is the rounded presentation of 19,780, so a reader cross-checking the two occurrences sees a 20 tok/s discrepancy.
fix_instruction: State the exact sustained-planning rate once (19,780 tok/s per host, 2,472.5 tok/s per GPU) and label the ~19,800 as its rounded presentation wherever the rounded form appears. Alternatively, use 19,780 consistently in the arithmetic and 19,800 only in prose, with a one-time parenthetical that the prose figure is rounded.

evidence: Table 3-3, printed p. 57: "the challenger's own 32L/4096H GQA (8 KV-heads × 128) = 0.131 MB/token at FP16 × 9,200 ≈ 1.20 GB". Earlier in §3.3.3, printed p. 45: "so 9,200 × 0.0655 MB ≈ 0.60 GB (≈1.2 GB at FP16)".
issue: The FP16 KV for the 32L/4096H GQA challenger is stated as ~1.20 GB in Table 3-3 but as ~1.2 GB in §3.3.3. The exact value from the table's own inputs is 9,200 × 131,072 B = 1,205,862,400 B = 1.2059 GB, which rounds to 1.21 GB, not 1.20 GB. Table 3-3's "≈ 1.20 GB" is a truncation; the prose's "≈1.2 GB" is a coarse rounding. Neither is the rounded value 1.21 GB. The 8-bit row has the same issue: 9,200 × 65,536 B = 602,931,200 B = 0.6029 GB, which the table prints as "≈ 0.60 GB" — also a truncation, not a rounding.
fix_instruction: In Table 3-3 and in §3.3.3, print the FP16 challenger KV as ~1.21 GB (1,205,862,400 B) and the 8-bit challenger KV as ~0.603 GB (602,931,200 B), or state explicitly that the 1.20 / 0.60 figures are truncations of the exact byte counts. Do not mix truncated table values with rounded prose values for the same quantity.

evidence: "9,500/7.08 ≈ 1,342 tok/s × 3600 ÷ $20 [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]" and "7.08 s = 1.08 s prefill + 6.0 s decode"
issue: Chapter 5 Table 5-2 uses a 6.0 s decode duration for the ~242,000 tokens/$ row, derived from a 20 ms/token rate (300 × 0.020 = 6.0 s), which is internally consistent. However, on the same page (p.112, §5.3.2), the reconciliation note states "~85% of 7.08 s on the illustrative 20 ms/token basis, where 7.08 s = 1.08 s prefill + 6.0 s decode; ~87% of 8.58 s on the canonical 25 ms/token basis." The 85% figure (6.0/7.08 = 84.7%) and 87% figure (7.5/8.58 = 87.4%) both check out arithmetically. However, the text elsewhere in Ch 4 (p.86) states "~87% of the ~8.58 s window: 7.5 ÷ 8.58 = 87.4%" as the decode wall-clock share without qualifying it as operating-point-dependent in the same way. These are not contradictions per se, but Ch 5's note that "the two percentages are decode shares at two different operating points and should not be compared as if they were one series" is an unusual defensive clarification that suggests the author recognized potential confusion. This is borderline and may not be a true defect.
fix_instruction: If considered a defect: add a cross-reference in Ch 4 §3 (p.86) pointing to Ch 5's reconciliation note so the reader sees the two operating points are explicitly distinguished there too.

evidence: "Output tokens per dollar (single-stream decode, 50 tok/s) | 9,000 output tokens per dollar | 50 tok/s × 3600 s/hr ÷ $20/hr [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]"

evidence: "It is on the order of ~256 KiB (0.26 MB) per token at 8-bit for a 7B-class model (32 layers, d_hidden 4096, full-MHA) and ~1.25 MiB (1.31 MB) per token at 8-bit (~2.5 MiB, 2.62 MB at FP16) for a 70B-class model"
issue: This sentence mixes binary (MiB) and decimal (MB) units within a single parenthetical construction for the 70B case: '~1.25 MiB (1.31 MB) per token at 8-bit (~2.5 MiB, 2.62 MB at FP16)'. The reader must parse four numbers (1.25, 1.31, 2.5, 2.62) in two unit systems within one parenthesis. While each individual conversion is correct (1,310,720 B = 1.25 MiB = 1.31 MB; 2,621,440 B = 2.5 MiB = 2.62 MB), the presentation requires careful parsing and risks the reader comparing 1.25 MiB to 2.5 MiB as decimal MB. The book's stated SI convention (K=1,000, M=1,000,000, Ch 4) would suggest leading with the decimal MB values.
fix_instruction: Rewrite as '~1.31 MB (1.25 MiB) per token at 8-bit … ~2.62 MB (2.5 MiB) at FP16' to lead with the book's SI convention unit.

evidence: "The two-point approximation of the mean is E[L] ≈ 0.99 × 0.8 + 0.01 × 5.0 ≈ 0.84 s — looks fine."
issue: The arithmetic 0.99 × 0.8 + 0.01 × 5.0 = 0.792 + 0.050 = 0.842 s, which the text rounds to '≈0.84 s'. The next paragraph then gives three further values: the 'analytic mean of the mixture as specified' at ≈0.848 s and the 'sample mean' at 0.85 s. The display '≈0.84 s' is stated first and prominently as the 'two-point approximation', but 0.842 truncated to two decimals is 0.84, while rounded is 0.84 — so the displayed value is a truncation of 0.842. The text explicitly acknowledges this by giving three values and explaining each, so the arithmetic is correct. However, the '≈0.84 s' label on a value of 0.842 could be read as rounding when it is truncation (the figure on p.126 shows 'mean = 0.85s'). Not a computational error but a presentational inconsistency: the figure displays 0.85 (sample mean) while the prose opens with 0.84 (two-point approximation).
fix_instruction: In the opening sentence of §6.3.1, write '≈0.842 s' or add '(the sample mean, shown in Fig. 6.2, is 0.85 s)' to prevent the reader from thinking 0.84 and 0.85 are the same number.

evidence: "Decode: bandwidth verdict, canonical 8×H100 host (TP = 8) | weight-read bandwidth not binding at this operating point | 700 GB/s < 3.35 TB/s → the shard streams in ~5.2 ms at peak, 21% of the 25 ms TPOT step" and "Decode: required bandwidth, hypothetical single-device aggregate (TPOT ~25 ms) | 5.6 TB/s | 140 GB / 0.025 s"
issue: Table 6-1 (p.131) states for decode: '(b) achieved HBM utilization on the canonical host: 0.70 TB/s ÷ 3.35 TB/s = 20.9% per GPU, so weight-read bandwidth is not binding at the canonical point.' The 20.9% figure (0.70/3.35 = 0.20896) and the 21% figure in Ch 2 (5.2/25 = 0.208) are the same quantity expressed two ways (bandwidth fraction vs time fraction), both correct. The phrasing is correct but the unit ('% of TB/s') mixes a dimensionless percentage with a rate unit in a way that could confuse. This is minor prose clarity.
fix_instruction: Change '~21% of 3.35 TB/s' to '~21% of peak (0.70 TB/s)' in Table 6-1's Resource tell column.

evidence: "At 9.2K input tokens the canonical FP16 KV per request is ~24.1 GB on the input-only basis — 9,200 × 2,621,440 B = 24,117,248,000 B ≈ 24.12 GB"
issue: 9,200 × 2,621,440 = 24,117,248,000. 24,117,248,000 / 1,000,000,000 = 24.117248 GB, which rounds to 24.12 GB at two decimal places. The text states '≈24.12 GB'. This is correct. evidence: "per-request API list cost falls from $0.01164 to ≈$0.0030 — the input leg goes from 9,200 × $1.20/1M = $0.01104 to 2,000 × $1.20/1M = $0.00240 while the output leg stays 300 × $2.00/1M = $0.0006, so the total moves $0.01164 → ≈$0.0030, a ~3.9× reduction ($0.01164 ÷ $0.0030 = 3.88)"

However, the original total $0.01164 = $0.01104 + $0.00060 = $0.01164 exactly, so the original is exact while the reduced is rounded to $0.0030 (from $0.00300). The ratio 0.01164/0.00300 = 3.88 exactly. All arithmetic verified correct — no defect.

evidence: "n_hosts = ⌈50 rps × 8.6 s / 17 slots⌉ = ⌈430/17⌉ = ⌈25.29⌉ = 26 hosts (full utilization)"

evidence: "A prefill-throughput cross-check from the Chapter 8 model bounds it from below: 50 rps × 9,200 input = 460,000 prefill tokens/s ÷ ~19,800 tokens/s per host … = 24 hosts (460,000 ÷ 19,800 = 23.23, ceiled to a whole host)"

evidence: "weight-only arithmetic intensity ≈ 9,200 FLOP/byte — an upper bound that omits the ~24 GB KV write; adding that write to the denominator lowers the intensity to ≈ 7,850 FLOP/byte"

Adding ~24 GB KV write to denominator: total bytes = 140 + 24 = 164 GB = 1.64×10^11 B. 1.29×10^15 / 1.64×10^11 = 7,866 ≈ 7,850. Close enough (the text says ≈7,850, actual is 7,866 — a 0.2% difference, within the '≈' tolerance). Correct. Arithmetic verified — no defect.

evidence: "Compute ratio vs dense 70B | ~0.183× (≈18% of dense 70B compute) | (12.8B × 2) ÷ (70B × 2) = 25.6 GFLOP ÷ 140 GFLOP ≈ 0.183×"

If the query varies, the 1,200 token block is NOT byte-identical across requests unless the system prompt is distinct from the user query. If only the system instruction part is cached, the percentage would be much lower. Using 13% assumes the entire 1,200 token input is static, which contradicts the nature of a Q&A prompt.
fix_instruction: Clarify whether the 1,200 "prompt" tokens are static system instructions or dynamic user questions. If dynamic, the prefix caching saving is overstated. Correct the 13% figure or the definition of the cached prefix.
